featured_videos.title: The #1 Fat Mistake on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Eric Westman - Adapt Your Life
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Westman's hitting on something real here, and the comments show people are getting tired of the "fat is free real estate" messaging. There's a difference between eating enough fat to feel satiated and turning carnivore into a fat-eating competition, which honestly defeats the purpose for anyone doing this for weight loss. The stool marker thing sounds crude, but it's actually useful feedback that people ignore because they're too busy chasing macros on their phone. If your body's telling you it can't handle what you're eating, that's not a badge of honor, that's information.

featured_videos.title: Eating This Way Never Gets Old | Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.creator: Tatiana Timofeyev
featured_videos.editorial_title: Eating This Way Never Gets Old | Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.commentary: The "it gets old" comment always pops up, and honestly, I think it misses what actually matters. The people I've coached who stick with this aren't the ones eating fancy power bowls or trying to make it feel like something it's not. They're the ones who found their three or four meals they genuinely like and stopped performing for the camera. Tatiana's showing real food here. wings, broth, eggs. and that's the whole point. It doesn't have to be Instagram-worthy to work. What keeps this sustainable for most people is the opposite: boring repetition, salt handy, and zero thinking about what's for dinner.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore on a Budget: What to Buy at Dollar General
featured_videos.creator: KenDBerryMD
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore on a Budget: What to Buy at Dollar General
featured_videos.commentary: Here's what's jumping out at me from this video: the community isn't just celebrating the budget angle, they're celebrating permission. That 52-year-old guy posting about 22 pounds down in 48 days isn't just sharing a win, he's saying "this actually works and it doesn't require money I don't have." The comments keep coming back to the same thing . people are tired of being told eating well costs a fortune, and Dr. Berry's showing them it doesn't have to. The real story here isn't Dollar General, it's that when someone removes the excuse, the results follow.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore Is Too Expensive? Eat These 7 Foods
featured_videos.creator: Jenny Mitich
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore Is Too Expensive? Eat These 7 Foods
featured_videos.commentary: Ground beef and eggs will never be glamorous, and that's exactly why they work. I've been coaching long enough to know that the people who stick with carnivore aren't the ones eating grass-fed ribeye every night, they're the ones who figured out how to make a Tuesday dinner from what's on sale at Costco. One comment really stuck with me: someone's been doing $5.62 a day for two years and healed from eight diagnosed diseases. That's not despite the budget cuts, that's the actual eating pattern that's sustainable enough to change anything. The real win isn't the seven foods Jenny listed, it's understanding that cheap animal foods work just as well as expensive ones. Your body doesn't know if that ground beef cost $6 or $16 a pound.

featured_videos.title: The Carnivore Meal I’ll Make EVERY Week (Cheesy Meatball Bake)
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Carnivore Meal I’ll Make EVERY Week (Cheesy Meatball Bake)
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here tell you everything you need to know: people aren't watching for a pristine kitchen or a perfect setup. They're watching because the recipe works and the person making it is honest about how real cooking happens. That meatball bake is the kind of protocol I'd actually run week to week, too. Ground meat, cheese, cream, ghee in the pan to catch the fond. No overthinking. The batch-cooking tip in the comments is solid though, whoever said that knows what they're talking about. Five and four cook better than eight and one because heat moves through evenly. If you're prepping for the week, that's the detail that keeps your meal prep from becoming a frustration you skip.

featured_videos.title: Is the Carnivore Diet Actually Safe? New Research Explained
featured_videos.creator: Simnett Nutrition
featured_videos.editorial_title: Is the Carnivore Diet Actually Safe? New Research Explained
featured_videos.commentary: Derek's doing what everyone should do with nutrition research: showing the actual limits of the studies instead of pretending we have all the answers. That comment about "the flaws apply to almost all diet studies" is spot on, and it's exactly why I tell people to watch how they *feel* alongside the labs, not instead of them. The science on carnivore long-term doesn't exist yet because nobody's funding a 10-year trial, so what we're really working with is short-term data, self-reports, and individual experience. That matters more than some people want to admit. If you're curious about the cholesterol piece specifically, I went deeper into what the research actually says about lipids, but the real question Derek's asking here is honest: we don't know everything, and pretending we do is what got us into trouble in the first place.
